strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: Makes headless.continue_once replay-safe for lost caller responses and returns one Rust-owned bounded next_route after the selected task outcome.
Uses HeadlessContinuationDecisionRecorded evidence plus a compact continuation lookup to replay the same selected task/run without duplicate decision or TaskRunning events.
Keeps replay, route classification, and all stop boundaries in Rust; routing never executes recovery, apply, verification retry, parent join, shell, git, network, or service actions.
Uses task.list progress_overview fingerprints and aggregate sequence as bounded post-step route context.

answers.strategic_capabilities: Advances headless_autonomous_development directly, supported by persistent_structured_ledger, runtime_permission_enforcement, progress_visualization, controlled_workspace_tools, and subtask_orchestration.
answers.new_capability: A caller can retry headless.continue_once with the same continuation_id after a prior decision and receive replayed=true with the same selected task/run handles, bounded task outcome when terminal, task_in_progress when still running, and one next_route.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: M11.1 records the decision before task.run but gives callers no runtime-owned way to recover a lost response or classify the next explicit route without reconstructing policy from task/run/proposal surfaces.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: Headless controllers would risk duplicate task execution or client-side route policy drift after lost responses, weakening long-running autonomous development.
answers.non_duplicative: Yes. M11.1 executes one selected task, M10.2 aggregates task progress, and M10.1 classifies single-run progress. M11.2 adds replay of prior continuation decisions and bounded post-step routing.
answers.no_new_rpc: Yes. The existing headless.continue_once method is extended; no new RPC is added.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. The new next_route is bounded result metadata on an execution/replay contract, not a report, digest, history, verdict, readiness wrapper, or preview-only surface.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: Rust detects prior continuation decisions, prevents duplicate selection and TaskRunning evidence, reconstructs bounded selected-task outcomes, and classifies the next explicit route.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: It lets scheduled/headless callers safely recover from response loss and decide the next explicit recovery/apply/verifier/parent/progress step using runtime-owned route metadata.
answers.milestone_progress: M11 gains a replay-safe single-step primitive that can be composed into later bounded multi-step continuation without introducing a background scheduler.

guard_engine_change_review.review_intent: M11.2 changes the deterministic current phase manifest and adds an archived M11.2 manifest. Review must confirm replay-safe continuation behavior and bounded route metadata, not a wrapper or guard-only phase.

exit_criteria: headless.continue_once with an existing continuation_id returns replayed=true without selecting a new task
Replay does not append duplicate HeadlessContinuationDecisionRecorded or TaskRunning evidence
A still-running selected task returns status task_in_progress and next_route.kind inspect_progress_overview
A terminal selected task reconstructs bounded TaskRunResult evidence when available
Failed verifier-gate outcomes route to start_verification_recovery_explicitly
Recovery proposal outcomes route to review_and_authorize_recovery_proposal when bounded proposal evidence exists
Parent-join-ready outcomes route to run_parent_task_explicitly without executing parent join
VSIX validates next_route but does not own route policy
No raw prompt, provider response, file content, ledger payload, stdout, stderr, command, environment, path, request body, secret, or arbitrary percentage is stored or returned

test_tokens: creates a headless.continue_once request without owning selection policy

next_phase_candidate_notes: M11.3 may authorize a small bounded number of sequential continuation steps, but must stop at explicit recovery/apply/verifier/parent-join boundaries.
